{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfQnWESQ7hfSPK232xSGQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I have no reliable speedup from this attempt. The rest looks like L1↔L2 traffic on the output buffers: the benchmark's 64 instances write at a 1 KB stride, which aliases into half the L1 sets. That is a hypothesis from reading the code; I couldn't confirm it with counters. Earlier attempts tried to hide it with prefetch, so I changed the loop structure instead.\n\n- **First variant (load-all, compute-all, store-all in 4-line batches):** slower on all three opcodes, at 0.82x (add), 0.90x (sub) and 0.85x (mul).\n- **Second variant (the tree as it stands):** one vector per iteration, load, op and store chained, so the stores are spread evenly.\n\n**Second variant results.**\n\n| Run | op_add | op_sub | op_mul |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | 1.59x | 1.17x | 1.94x |\n| 2 | 0.94x | 1.28x | 1.79x |\n\nThe \"current\" baseline in the same check swings between 12 and 24 ns for identical code, so these ratios are not reliable. The new kernel's own times stay at 12–14 ns, the same as the accepted 12.4 ns. In run 2, op_add came out slower than the baseline, so this may still be rejected under the rule that no opcode may get slower. The compiler also still does not inline the AVX2 kernels into the opcode bodies, because their target attribute differs from the caller's.\n\nI left the working tree with the one-vector-per-iteration kernels and did not commit. I also made one stray no-op `echo` call to the shell, outside the check command, and it had no effect on the tree.\n\nNon-temporal stores would probably beat the baseline in this benchmark. I didn't ship them: the next opcode in a real graph reads the output straight back from DRAM, and NT stores need a fence before another thread can safely see them.\n\nIDEA: L1↔L2 read-for-ownership and eviction traffic on aliased output buffers -> replaced the 2x-unrolled kernels with one-vector-per-iteration load/op/store loops (a 4-line batched-store variant was 0.82–0.90x; the final variant showed 0.94–1.94x, but the baseline itself swung 12–24 ns, so it is not a reliable gain)"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":709,"cache_read_input_tokens":46796,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":709},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"82fb7cbe-f8dc-441c-bb6c-b7418ee026b6","uuid":"59f1b9dc-61b0-4d67-8f71-04d55ceee5cc","timestamp":"2026-09-25T20:25:58.533Z","request_id":"req_011CfQnWDeXCFW4iMHVvYfyJ"}
